label: ZHUANGZI · ANCIENT CHINA
title: Why this cook's knife never went dull.
sub: A Taoist secret about hard work.

label: I · THE COOK
title: A cook named Ding carved an ox for Lord Wenhui.
sub: Every move flowed like a dance.

label: II · CUT OR HACK
title: A good cook changes his knife once a year, because he cuts.
sub: Average cooks hack. New knife every month.

label: III · THE SAME BLADE
title: Ding kept one knife nineteen years, through thousands of oxen.

label: IV · THE GAPS
title: He never forced the blade. He slid it through the spaces between the joints.

label: V · THE HARD PART
title: At a tough spot, he slowed down, watched closely, and moved gently.
sub: Then it came apart like a clod of earth.

label: VI · THE LESSON
title: Lord Wenhui said this taught him how to care for life.

label: ZHUANGZI
title: Work with the grain, not against it.
sub: Save this for your hardest week.
